records.title: Aalto University — Design System
records.summary: Aalto Design System is the unified framework of Aalto University for building clear, consistent digital sites and services. It documents the digital resources, UI elements, and instructions that teams use across the university’s ecosystem. It’s built in a way that helps teams stay consistent without overthinking it: tokens as the foundation, then components, modules, sections, and templates that scale up to page layouts. Tokens define reusable visual values across channels, and templates provide consistent page structures for common use cases.

records.title: Adobe — Spectrum
records.summary: Spectrum is a Design System developed by Adobe that provides components and tools to enhance the productivity of product teams and create a cohesive experience across Adobe applications. The development of Spectrum is guided by foundational principles. Spectrum offers open-source implementations such as Spectrum CSS, React Spectrum, and Spectrum Web Components, along with detailed usage guidelines. This enables developers to effectively integrate the design system. UI kits are currently only available in Adobe XD.

records.summary: Ant Design is Ant Group's Design System made for teams building big, data-heavy products. Guidelines include all the necessary information about platforms, foundations, patterns, components, inputs, and technologies.

records.summary: The CMS Design System is maintained by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to build Section 508 compliant, accessible interfaces across Medicare, Medicaid, and Healthcare.gov. CMS built its own React components and CSS utilities on top of the U.S. Web Design System (USWDS) , plus a grid framework for federal healthcare products. Elastic includes extensive accessibility and writing guidelines in its documentation, ensuring user-friendly and inclusive design practices.

records.title: GitHub — Primer
records.summary: Primer is a design system developed by GitHub for designing interfaces. It provides a collection of open source principles, standards, and recommendations. Primer's guidelines offer a common grammar and vocabulary to build projects. There are best practices for hierarchy, readability, accessibility, and responsive design. The guidelines are detailed, with interesting examples and use cases provided. For components, there are React and Rails examples, as well as component configuration settings and variants in Figma.

records.title: Meta — Astryx
records.summary: Astryx is an open source design system from Meta that helps product teams build and ship interfaces faster. It provides a library of accessible, themeable React components, ready to use page templates for common pages, and fully customizable themes that adapt to any brand. Astryx design system is also agent and AI ready, with support for scaffolding projects, generating themes, and accessing documentation from the command line or through MCP. Built and refined inside Meta, the design system is open source on GitHub.

records.title: U.S. Web — Design System
records.summary: The U.S. Web Design System (USWDS) is the federal government's answer to making digital life easier for everyday Americans. This system gives government web developers the tools they need—everything from color schemes to button designs—to build sites that actually work for real people. The goal is simple: make government websites consistent, accessible, and efficient. Hundreds of teams across all levels of government use it, improving it based on how people actually interact with their sites. It's a rare example of government tech that evolves through genuine public collaboration.

records.title: Component overview: Accordion
records.summary: Accordion is a vertically stacked set of expandable panels, each containing a header and an associated content area. It allows users to view a summary or a condensed version of the content and then expand it to reveal detailed information. Accordions are typically used when screen real estate is limited, and there's a need to manage the visibility of large amounts of content. They enhance the user experience by presenting information in a structured, efficient way, allowing users to access details on demand without navigating away from the current context.
